Yes — one thing, and it's the one that actually matters: **the #61 fix has never been exercised.** Everything else is confirmed.

You don't need to wait 20 minutes for the display to sleep on its own. `pmset displaysleepnow` fires the exact trigger we identified — display off → powerd drops "prevent sleep while display is on" → coreaudiod tears down its audio contexts ~19s later → config change. That's what killed it 6 times.

Install v0.3.2 first (the menu should read `LaughCounter v0.3.2 (6)`), make sure it's listening, then:

```bash
LOG="$HOME/Library/Application Support/LaughCounter/laughcounter.log"
BEFORE=$(ls ~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/ 2>/dev/null | grep -ci laugh)
echo "=== before ==="; tail -3 "$LOG"; echo "crash reports: $BEFORE"

pmset displaysleepnow      # screen goes dark; wake it whenever you like
sleep 90

echo "=== after ==="; tail -8 "$LOG"
AFTER=$(ls ~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/ 2>/dev/null | grep -ci laugh)
echo "crash reports: $BEFORE -> $AFTER"
pgrep -x LaughCounter >/dev/null && echo "STILL RUNNING ✅" || echo "NOT RUNNING ❌"
```

About 90 seconds. What the outcomes mean:

- **`audio configuration changed — reconfiguring` followed by `listening started`, count unchanged, STILL RUNNING** → fixed. The whole thing is done and I'll close it out.
- **`configuration changed` with nothing after it, count +1, NOT RUNNING** → still crashing. Send me the new `.ips` top frames (`grep -o '"symbol":"[^"]*"' <file> | head -12`) and I'll work from that.
- **No `configuration changed` line at all** → the teardown didn't fire in 90s. Either re-run with a longer `sleep`, or use the other reliable trigger: System Settings → Sound → Input, switch to a different device and back. That fires the same notification.

Worth noting one possible middle outcome: `configuration changed` → `could not start listening: …` → then a retry, then `listening started`. That's also a pass — it means the Obj-C trap or the format guard caught something and the retry ladder recovered, which is the designed behaviour rather than a failure.

> ⚠️ Just this one test outstanding. Everything else from this session is landed and released: the crash fix (v0.3.0/v0.3.1), the standby resume, Pause listening, and the version in the menu (v0.3.2). The two long-standing items ([#26](https://github.com/missingbulb/LaughCounter/issues/26) signing, [#25](https://github.com/missingbulb/LaughCounter/issues/25) setup script) need you rather than me, and [#72](https://github.com/missingbulb/LaughCounter/issues/72) (the CI test target) is queued for whenever you want it.

content.text:
That is a genuinely good result, and it changes what we know.

**The fatal bug is gone.** Crash reports `6 → 6`, `STILL RUNNING ✅`. The same exception that killed the app 6 times — `required condition is false: format.sampleRate == inputHWFormat.sampleRate` — now appears as a logged error line and the app carries on.

**And the Obj-C trap works.** That log line's shape, `com.apple.coreaudio.avfaudio: required condition is false: …`, is exactly what `ObjCExceptionTrap` builds from `exception.name` + `exception.reason`. So an `NSException` did unwind through the intervening Swift closure frame and get caught. That was the open question I'd flagged as unproven twice; it's now answered empirically, and it's what saved the process here.

**But my root-cause theory for #61 was wrong.** I said a stale engine cache made `outputFormat` disagree with `inputHWFormat`, and that a fresh engine would make them agree. A fresh engine is being built on every one of those attempts, and they still disagree. So the rebuild wasn't the fix — the trap was.

What the evidence actually says: `AudioHub` checks `inputNode.outputFormat(forBus: 0)` in both `prepareFormat()` and `start()`, and **both checks passed** — otherwise you'd see my `input device changed between prepare and start` error instead of the exception. Yet AVFoundation then compared against `inputHWFormat` and found a mismatch. That means `outputFormat(forBus:0)` is simply not the hardware format. For an input node, `inputFormat(forBus: 0)` is. With the BRIO torn down, `inputFormat` is 0 Hz while `outputFormat` still reports a plausible 48000 — so my "is the mic ready?" guard was reading a property that can't tell me the mic is gone, and waved through a start that could never work.

The fix is to read `inputFormat(forBus: 0)` as the source of truth, and refuse to install the tap unless it's valid *and* agrees with `outputFormat` — so `installTap` is never reached in the mismatch state at all.

One thing I need before I ship it, so I size the retry ladder from data instead of guessing again:

```bash
tail -12 "$HOME/Library/Application Support/LaughCounter/laughcounter.log"
```

Your output ended at *"retrying in 32s (attempt 5 of 5)"*, so I can't see whether that last attempt recovered. If it did, the ladder is fine and only the format check needs fixing. If it gave up, the ladder is too short — we saw the BRIO stay away about 7 minutes once, and 5 attempts only spans ~62 seconds.

(Also: `zsh: command not found: wake` was my fault — interactive zsh doesn't treat `#` as a comment by default, so my inline note ran as a command. Harmless, `pmset` and `sleep` both ran. I'll keep comments out of pasted scripts.)

> ⚠️ Where things stand:
> - ✅ **No more crashes, no more wedged mic.** The worst failure mode — process dies, `applicationWillTerminate` skipped, BRIO dead until re-plugged — is fixed and verified on your machine.

input.body:
Measured on the owner's Mac mini with v0.3.2, using `pmset displaysleepnow` as the trigger. **No crash and no wedged mic** — #61/#72 hold, and the `ObjCExceptionTrap` demonstrably caught the `NSException` (an open question until now). But capture stays down for the entire display-sleep window.

```
10:49:12 ERROR could not start listening: com.apple.coreaudio.avfaudio: required condition is false: format.sampleRate == inputHWFormat.sampleRate
…            (attempts 2–5, ~62s of ladder)
10:50:06 ERROR listening still down after 5 retries — reconnect the microphone and use "Start listening" in the menu
11:18:47 INFO  displays woke while listening was down — resuming listening shortly
11:18:50 INFO  audio configuration changed — reconfiguring
11:18:50 INFO  listening started (sampleRate=48000, channels=2)
```

Recovery did happen — 28 minutes later, when the displays woke and the device came back. So the remaining problems are narrower than "it doesn't recover".

## 1. `AudioHub` reads the wrong format property

Both guards check `inputNode.outputFormat(forBus: 0)`, and **both passed** on every failed attempt — otherwise the log would show `input device changed between prepare and start` rather than the exception. AVFoundation then compared against `inputHWFormat` and disagreed.

`outputFormat(forBus:0)` is the bus's output format, not the hardware's. With the device torn down it still reports a plausible 48 kHz, while `inputFormat(forBus: 0)` — the hardware format, the one `installTap` asserts on — correctly reports 0. So the readiness check could not detect an absent microphone, and waved through starts that could never succeed, leaving `installTap` to raise.

Fix: read `inputFormat(forBus: 0)` as the source of truth, and require it to agree with `outputFormat` before installing the tap. `installTap` is then never reached in the mismatch state, and an absent device throws a clean error instead of relying on the exception trap for routine control flow.

## 2. The retry ladder gives up while the cause is still present

Five attempts spanning ~62 seconds, against a device that was unavailable for 28 minutes. Giving up is wrong here: the condition is temporary and self-resolving, and nothing guarantees a notification on return (recovery happened to arrive via a configuration change, but the backstop attempt at 11:18:48 fired first and failed).

Fix: double to a 60s ceiling and keep checking for as long as the counter is meant to be on, instead of stopping after five. With fix 1 each check is a cheap format read that throws before touching the tap — one a minute is far below any rate that could wedge a USB mic. Log the first few attempts, announce the switch to slow checking once, then stay quiet until it succeeds.

## 3. The give-up message gives wrong advice

*"reconnect the microphone"* — nothing is wrong with the microphone; the displays are asleep. It also logged twice (again on the backstop attempt, since a backstop deliberately doesn't reset the failure streak).

## Out of scope, needs an owner decision

`displaysleep 20` means **counting stops ~20 minutes into a movie** on this hardware, because the input device goes with the display. The *Keep Mac awake while listening* option holds `.idleSystemSleepDisabled` only, explicitly letting the display sleep on the theory that audio keeps running — which these measurements show is false here. Making it also hold `.idleDisplaySleepDisabled` would keep counting at the cost of a lit screen in a living room at night. Filed separately rather than decided here.

# LaughCounter for macOS (native menu-bar app)

The clean way to run LaughCounter on a Mac: a tiny menu-bar app that uses only
**built-in macOS frameworks** — nothing to install, nothing left behind.

- **Detects laughter** with Apple's built-in Sound Analysis (no model download).
- **Counts** distinct laughs and **logs** them to
  `~/Library/Application Support/LaughCounter/laughs.jsonl` (no audio saved).
- **😄 menu-bar icon** shows today's count — that's your "it's running" light.
- **A soft blip** plays when a laugh is logged.
- **Say “I just laughed”** and it logs a laugh it missed, blipping **twice** to
  confirm (on-device speech recognition — nothing leaves your Mac). There's also a
  menu item / ⌘L if you'd rather click.

## Get it (no Xcode needed)

**⬇️ [Download the latest LaughCounter.dmg](https://github.com/missingbulb/LaughCounter/releases/latest/download/LaughCounter.dmg)** — this link always points at the most recent published release.

Prefer a specific build, or no release published yet? The app is also built for
every change by GitHub Actions on a macOS runner:

1. Go to the repo's **Actions** tab → open the latest **“Build macOS DMG”** run.
2. Download the **`LaughCounter-dmg`** artifact and unzip it to get `LaughCounter.dmg`.

*(Releases are published by pushing a `v*` tag — see “Cutting a release” below.)*

## Install

1. Open `LaughCounter.dmg` and drag **LaughCounter** into **Applications**.
2. **Get past Gatekeeper (first launch only).** The app is ad-hoc signed but not
   notarized (that needs a paid Apple Developer account), so macOS blocks the first
   open with *“Apple could not verify LaughCounter is free of malware.”* Clear it
   **one of two ways**:
   - **System Settings:** click **Done** on the warning, then open **System
     Settings → Privacy & Security**, scroll to **Security**, and click **Open
     Anyway** next to *“LaughCounter was blocked…”*. Confirm **Open Anyway** again.
   - **Terminal (most reliable):** after dragging it to Applications, run
     `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/LaughCounter.app`, then open it
     normally.

   > On **macOS 15 (Sequoia)** the old **right-click → Open** shortcut no longer
   > bypasses this — you must use one of the two methods above.
3. Approve **Microphone** and **Speech Recognition** when prompted.
4. A 😄 with a number appears in your menu bar. That's it.

**Always-on:** add it to **System Settings → General → Login Items** so it starts
with the Mac. **Uninstall:** quit it, drag the app to the Trash, and (optionally)
delete `~/Library/Application Support/LaughCounter/`.

## Build it yourself (optional, on a Mac)

```bash
cd mac
bash scripts/build-app.sh     # -> dist/LaughCounter.app  (bakes AppIcon.icns)
bash scripts/make-dmg.sh      # -> dist/LaughCounter.dmg  (with the 😄 volume icon)
```

Requires the Swift toolchain (Xcode Command Line Tools). No third-party packages,
and no toolchain beyond what macOS ships. The committed `Resources/AppIcon.png`
master is turned into a multi-resolution `.icns` at build time with
`sips`/`iconutil` — replace that PNG to change the icon.

This produces an **ad-hoc-signed** app (the Gatekeeper step under *Install*
applies). To instead sign it with a real **Developer ID** and notarize it — so it
opens with no warning — you need a paid Apple Developer account, then:

```bash
export MACOS_SIGN_IDENTITY="Developer ID Application: Your Name (TEAMID)"
bash scripts/build-app.sh          # signs with Hardened Runtime + entitlements
bash scripts/make-dmg.sh
export APPLE_ID=you@example.com APPLE_TEAM_ID=XXXXXXXXXX APPLE_APP_PASSWORD=xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx
bash scripts/notarize-dmg.sh       # submits to Apple + staples the ticket
```

Both DMG workflows do this automatically when the matching repository secrets are
set (`MACOS_CERT_P12`, `MACOS_CERT_PASSWORD`, `MACOS_SIGN_IDENTITY`, `APPLE_ID`,
`APPLE_TEAM_ID`, `APPLE_APP_PASSWORD`) — so published releases open with no
warning. This is the **non–App Store** path; a Mac App Store build additionally
requires the App Sandbox and a different (Apple Distribution) certificate.

## Cutting a release

Releases publish **automatically**. On every push to `main` that touches `mac/**`,
the **Release macOS DMG** workflow builds the app, packages the DMG, and
creates/updates the GitHub Release for the app's current version (read from
`Info.plist`), attaching `LaughCounter.dmg` — which is what the
[latest-release download link](https://github.com/missingbulb/LaughCounter/releases/latest/download/LaughCounter.dmg)
resolves to.

So to **ship a new version**, bump `CFBundleShortVersionString` in
`Resources/Info.plist` and merge to `main` — a new `v<version>` Release appears on
its own. (Merges that keep the same version just refresh that Release's DMG.) You
can also publish a Release from the GitHub UI, or run the workflow manually from
the Actions tab.

## The laugh log

Laughs are appended to `~/Library/Application Support/LaughCounter/laughs.jsonl`,
one JSON object per line, fields in a fixed order:

| field | meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `start_iso` | human-readable start time (ISO-8601) |
| `label` | `auto` (detected), `missed` (you told us we missed one), `candidate` (sub-threshold — logged for tuning, **not counted**), `rejected` (not counted) |
| `start` / `end` | epoch seconds of the laugh's real start/end (from the classifier's window timing) |
| `peak` | highest laughter confidence during the laugh (0–1, rounded) |
| `duration` | `end − start` in seconds. **Coarse:** the built-in classifier analyses in ~3s windows, so a single laugh reads ~3s; only laughs spanning several windows read longer. It's a rough length, not a precise one. |
| `mean` | average laughter confidence across the laugh |
| `source` | `mic` (auto), `voice` (spoken “I just laughed”), `button` (menu / ⌘L) |
| `origin` | you-vs-TV **hypothesis**: `me` or `tv` |
| `tv_signal` | strongest produced-audio context (0–1) the hypothesis is based on |
| `origin_reason` | plain-language why (e.g. `music=0.66 (soundtrack/audience) → TV`) |
| `type` | which laugh class fired (e.g. giggle, chuckle), when known |
| `context` | top competing non-laugh classes heard |

**You vs the TV (two counters).** The menu bar shows `😄 N  📺 M` — your laughs vs
the TV's, today. Each laugh gets a *hypothesis*, not a verdict: a strong
produced-audio context (music, dialogue, audience, instruments — `tv_signal ≥ 0.3`)
is attributed to the TV; clean laughter with little of that is attributed to you.
Only *your* laughs blip. It will guess wrong sometimes (a real laugh over TV music),
which is why every laugh is still logged with its reasoning — nothing is discarded.
The class-based classifier can't hear *who* laughed; a loudness/proximity signal and,
eventually, laugh enrollment would sharpen it.

**Sub-threshold logging:** anything that clears a deliberately low bar but not the
counting threshold is written with `label:"candidate"` (uncounted) — so near-misses
are on record and later “I laughed” feedback can be aligned to a nearby event.

**Which build am I running?** The menu's first line carries it —
`LaughCounter v0.3.2 (6)`. The number in brackets is the build: two DMGs can share
a version string when a change ships without a version bump, and the build number
is what tells them apart.

**Pause:** *Pause listening* (⌘P) stops counting and hands the microphone back
until you pick *Start listening* again — the menu shows `Status: paused` meanwhile.
It isn't remembered across launches: quitting and reopening starts it listening
again, which is what an always-on box should do after a power cut.

**Sleep & standby:** the mic is released when the Mac sleeps and picked back up
when it returns — from a short sleep or from a long standby, where the USB bus was
powered down and the mic takes a while to reappear (LaughCounter waits longer, then
retries with a widening gap for about a minute before giving up and telling you so
in the activity log). It resumes **only if the counter was running when the Mac went
to sleep**: sleep it while paused, or with the microphone never granted, and it
comes back off. A wake with nobody there (Power Nap, a screensaver dismissed)
doesn't restart anything that was already running.

**Activity log:** lifecycle events (started / slept / woke / reconfigured / errors)
and each laugh's hypothesis go to `laughcounter.log` next to the laugh log (open it
from the menu), so if listening ever stops — or a guess looks off — you can see why.

## Notes & limits

See [`../docs/DESIGN-AND-TRADEOFFS.md`](../docs/DESIGN-AND-TRADEOFFS.md) for the
full picture: how misses become improvements (threshold tuning now, a personalised
Create ML model later), the who-laughed plan, and the voice-command tradeoffs
(false triggers, on-device availability).

each attempt is a cheap format read that throws before touching the tap, and one

## `outputFormat` cannot tell you the microphone is gone

Both guards checked `inputNode.outputFormat(forBus: 0)` and **both passed** on every failed attempt — the log shows the `installTap` exception, not our own `input device changed between prepare and start` error.

`outputFormat(forBus:0)` is the bus's output format, not the hardware's. With the device torn down it still reports a plausible 48 kHz, while `inputFormat(forBus: 0)` — the format `installTap` actually asserts on — reports 0. So the readiness check could not detect an absent microphone at all.

`validatedFormat()` now reads `inputFormat` as the source of truth and requires it to agree with `outputFormat`, in both `prepareFormat()` and `start()`. An absent device throws a clean error, `installTap` is never reached in the mismatch state, and the trap goes back to being a backstop rather than routine control flow.

This also corrects the record on #61: I attributed the original crash to a stale engine cache and predicted a fresh engine would make the formats agree. They still disagree on a brand-new engine — the rebuild wasn't what fixed the crash, the trap was. The engine rebuild stays (it's correct hygiene across a device change), but the real defect was reading the wrong property.

Five attempts spanning ~62 seconds, against a cause that lasted 28 minutes — then it told the user to *"reconnect the microphone"*, which was fine all along. It now doubles to a 60s ceiling and keeps checking for as long as the counter is meant to be on. Each attempt is a cheap format read that throws before touching the tap, so one a minute is far below any rate that could cycle a USB mic. The switch to slow checking is announced once instead of a line a minute for half an hour.

Recovery in the measured run actually arrived via `.AVAudioEngineConfigurationChange` when the device returned — which also confirms the `AudioHub`-owned observer survives an engine rebuild. Registered against `audio.engine` from `AppDelegate`, as it was before #59, it would have gone quiet after the first restart and never fired.

- `dev/procedures/mac-audio-lifecycle.md` — the `inputFormat` vs `outputFormat` rule, and that the mic is unavailable for as long as the displays sleep.
- `mac/README.md` — rewritten *Sleep, standby & the sleeping display* note, including that *Keep Mac awake while listening* deliberately allows display sleep, so a long film needs display sleep turned off instead.

Version → **0.3.3**.

CI compiles it. The real check is the same one that produced this diagnosis: `pmset displaysleepnow`, wait, wake, and read the log. Expected now: one `no input hardware — the microphone is not available` line and one `input device still unavailable — checking every 60s`, then `listening started` when the displays wake — no exception lines, no *reconnect the microphone*.
